GOV.UK press release (DHSC, Alison McGovern MP and The Rt Hon Yvette Cooper MP): 'Government pledges earlier support to tackle mental health crises'. JSON-LD datePublished = dateModified = 2026-10-09T08:17:09+01:00 (08:17 BST today).
Response to the Independent Review into prevalence and support for mental health conditions, ADHD and autism (the Fonagy Review), published today 9 October. Chaired by Prof Peter Fonagy, vice chairs Prof Sir Simon Wessely and Prof Gillian Baird.
HEADLINE COMMITMENTS: support without waiting for a clinical diagnosis; a forthcoming Mental Health Strategy; strengthened regulation of ADHD and autism assessments, working towards making ALL diagnostic assessments a CQC-regulated activity (covering NHS-funded, non-NHS-funded and self-funding patients); a review of advertising practices; recommendation to ban direct-to-public advertising of NHS-funded ADHD and autism assessments.
KEY FINDING AS GOVERNMENT STATES IT: mental distress has increased substantially among children and young people, driven by social media, financial insecurity, uncertainty about the future, poorer sleep and reduced feelings of connection and belonging. 'While referrals and diagnoses for ADHD and autism have risen significantly, the review found that population-level prevalence of these conditions appears broadly stable.'
Alan Milburn's interim 'Young People and Work' review: among 16-25s not in education, employment or training, 24% cited depression or anxiety as their main limiting condition, 22% autism, 18% another mental illness.
Sits alongside the government's £4 billion package for children with special educational needs.
Yvette Cooper, Secretary of State for Health and Social Care: 'Professor Fonagy's review has shown the importance of early intervention to address mental health and neurodevelopmental conditions and the huge distress these can cause. It is clear that mental health services need to change to focus more on the early support young people need to stay in education or work or keep their lives on track.' And: 'we will also take action to strengthen the oversight of mental health and neurodevelopmental services, and make all diagnostic assessments for ADHD and autism CQC-regulated, so people can be confident that assessments are high quality and that the NHS is not being overcharged by independent or private providers.'
Prof Peter Fonagy, Head of the UCL Division of Psychology and Language Sciences: 'Our findings show a system under immense strain, where diagnosis has increasingly become a very narrow pathway to finding support for distress caused by complex and wide-ranging factors. This Review's recommendations offer a roadmap to shift from a diagnostic labelling model to a flexible, needs-led system.' And: 'Diagnosis remains essential and must be protected - what has to change is that it is no longer the only door through which help can be reached.'
Dr Nick Broughton, National Priority Programme Director for Mental Health, Learning Disability and Neurodevelopmental Conditions, NHS England/DHSC: 'This is a landmark moment for how we better understand the mental health needs across society.' Notes 'six million pupils now able to access NHS mental health support in schools'.
